solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hobo needs a large drink

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp, in American slang a bum
'a' as in 'five pounds a head' means per

explanation.surface: A tramp is in want of a big drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' does a quiet job here: in prices such as 'ten pence a pound' it means PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper is an old word for a glass filled to the brim, a toast drunk in full.

clue.text: Support Wolves? This might be checked at entrance to ground

definitions.text: This might be checked at entrance to ground

parts.note: to support someone is to back them
wolves hunt in a pack

explanation.surface: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers football club, so this reads as fans backing their team at the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: A football ground in Britain is a stadium; 'Wolves' as a club name is the misdirection, here it is simply the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards search rucksacks carried by fans as they come through the turnstiles of a stadium.

clue.text: Tycoon featured in publication, "name" getting worried

parts.note: MAG is short for magazine, a publication
worried in the sense of fretted, 'what's eating you?', gives ATE

explanation.surface: A business mogul appears in a magazine and their name is causing anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' is past tense of to worry at, gnaw: ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy, powerful businessperson, a synonym for a business mogul.

clue.text: Grand hospital department needing engineers in situation where things fall apart

parts.note: something grand in scale is epic
ENT is the Ear, Nose and Throat department
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A large hospital unit relies on engineers in a crisis where everything collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point on the surface above an earthquake's origin, where buildings tumble.

clue.text: Woman shows anger about nothing — she's one of these?

parts.note: Vi is a woman's name, short for Violet

indicators.note: about means going around, so the anger word surrounds the nothing

parts.note: someone who shows anger rages
O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A woman flies into a fury over nothing, so the clue asks whether she is a shrew.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural with -ES is less common than VIRAGOS but accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: Viragos are domineering, bad-tempered women, which the angry woman of the clue would be one of.

clue.text: Reading petition, ranter becomes unsettled

indicators.note: unsettled letters are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noisy protester gets agitated while reading a petition aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' looks like the act of perusing the petition; it is the definition, in the sense of one's take on something.
explanation.definitionFit: A reading of a text or event is a particular understanding or explanation of it.

clue.text: Pest upset Parliament, probing charity

indicators.note: something probing pushes into another thing, so it goes inside

parts.note: charity is aid given to those in need

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read from bottom up

parts.note: HP stands for the Houses of Parliament

explanation.surface: A troublemaker overturns Parliament while investigating a charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are sap-sucking insects that gardeners treat as pests.

clue.text: Male at party entertained by individual performing live

indicators.note: entertained as a guest is taken in, so it sits inside

parts.note: one is a single individual
a stag party is for men only, so a male guest is a stag

explanation.surface: A man at a party is amused by a single act playing in front of an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor appearing before an audience in the theatre is performing live in front of them.

clue.text: Aim to preserve a set of books in cabin

indicators.note: to preserve something is to keep it safe inside

parts.note: a shy is a throw or aim, as at a coconut shy
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone means to keep a library of books in a hut.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where you throw balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A shack or crude hut is a simple dwelling, much like a rough cabin.

clue.text: Phony presence felt as deception

indicators.note: phony means fake, so the letters are falsified into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fake air of authority is perceived as a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtaining goods by pretending to be what one is not is a legal kind of fraud or trickery.

clue.text: Clued-up company worker is about to celebrate retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to celebrate in song is to sing
the ant is the crossword's stock worker insect

explanation.surface: An informed employee of a firm is about to celebrate leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' sounds like the worker's leaving do but it turns SING into GNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clued-up is well informed and aware, which is what being cognisant of something means.

clue.text: Spray water on a book

parts.note: to hose something is to spray it with water

explanation.surface: A gardener hoses down a book.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the books of the Old Testament is named after this minor prophet.

clue.text: Note about film actors

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the note goes around the film

parts.note: PS is a postscript, a note added to a letter
a film is a thin layer, as of dust

explanation.surface: A short memo concerning a movie's cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Players is an old word for those who act on stage, as in a company of strolling performers.

clue.text: Notice one in angry discourse exuding heat?

indicators.note: in places one thing within another

parts.note: a rant is an angry tirade
an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An announcement in a heated tirade gives off warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiant heater gives out heat by radiation; the question mark flags that sense.

clue.text: Fiddle about, in need of passion

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
passion is heat, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: A violinist plays around, lacking emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' suggests a violin; it is the swindling sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle the accounts is to swindle or act dishonestly.

clue.text: Greek statesman has page and two men following

parts.note: two men's names side by side, Eric and Les, as in the comedians Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: An ancient Athenian leader has an attendant and two men behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two men' gives two names; ERIC and LES are the comic duo Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: This leader dominated Athens in its golden age of the fifth century BC.

clue.text: Supply of wine drunk by long-term professional soldier

indicators.note: drunk by means swallowed, so it goes inside

parts.note: a career soldier or diplomat is a long-term professional
a wine bin is a rack or store of bottles

explanation.surface: A stock of wine downed by a seasoned military man.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbineer is a soldier armed with a carbine, a short rifle.

clue.text: Old revolutionary caught by trick, a financial problem

indicators.note: caught by means held inside

parts.note: a trap is a trick to catch someone

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: old means aged

explanation.surface: A veteran radical is snared by a ruse, a money headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old revolutionary' suggests Che or Lenin; 'revolutionary' just reverses AGED to DEGA.
explanation.definitionFit: When a country's imports exceed its exports the shortfall is an economic worry.

clue.text: Most stylish sixties film? There's something wet about it

indicators.note: about means around, so the wet weather wraps around the film

parts.note: sleet is wet falling snow
Kes is a 1969 Ken Loach film about a boy and a kestrel

explanation.surface: Asking which sixties film is the smartest, with rain around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek describes smooth, elegant styling, so the superlative is most elegant.

clue.text: Halt, stopping short, with awful rain in sheets

indicators.note: stopping short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: halt is an old word for lame

indicators.note: awful letters are in a bad state, jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something grinds to a halt early in horrible rain falling in sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halt' looks like stop, but is the old adjective meaning lame; 'stopping short' cuts LAME to LAM, and 'awful' gives INAR from RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Laminar flow moves in smooth parallel layers, like thin plates stacked together.

clue.text: Game backed by man of nonsense, not a leader

indicators.note: backed by means followed by

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter goes

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse

explanation.surface: A sport is supported by a nonsense writer who is no captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a leader' looks like the definition; 'not a' removes A from LEAR and 'leader' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler governs a country, as a monarch or chief does.

clue.text: Element of humility not unknown after thrashing

indicators.note: thrashing beats the letters into a new order
not means without, so the letter goes

parts.note: in algebra y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: An element of humility is lost after a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' removes Y from HUMILITY, and 'after thrashing' rearranges HUMILIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithium is the third chemical element, a light alkali metal used in batteries.

clue.text: Journalist, having travelled in, is worn out

indicators.note: in places one thing within another

parts.note: ED is short for editor
having travelled on horseback is having rode, simple past rode

explanation.surface: A reporter who has been on a journey is exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Eroded rock has been gradually worn away by wind and water.

clue.text: Chief's tucked into eggs and lettuce

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
chief means main; the 's is 'is' joining it to the rest

explanation.surface: The boss is tucking into eggs and salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests the boss eating; here it is a containment signal, and 'Chief's' carries an 's meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: Romaine is the American name for cos, a long-leaved salad variety.

clue.text: Keen on including composer's last piece of music

indicators.note: including means holding inside

parts.note: into is slang for keen on

indicators.note: last means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fan enjoys the composer's final work.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an opening passage leading into a song.

clue.text: Article, coloured on the outside with a stain

indicators.note: being on the outside means wrapping around the other piece

parts.note: tinted means coloured
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A thing was coloured outside, it has a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Tainted means spoiled or marked, as with contamination.

clue.text: Cook, enthusiast for sweet American cake

parts.note: to do something is to cook it, as in 'done to a turn'
a nut is an enthusiast, as in fitness nut

explanation.surface: A chef who loves sweet things fancies a US cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling is signalled; British 'doughnut'.
explanation.definitionFit: A US doughnut is a fried ring of sweetened dough.

clue.text: Remain close when protecting old group hiding away

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping around

parts.note: to cling is to stay close
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Staying near a former team that is in hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Closeting is shutting someone away in private, out of sight.

clue.text: Sleepy type beginning to moan when instruction to wake up comes round

indicators.note: comes round means surrounding the other piece

parts.note: 'do rouse!' is an order to wake

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A drowsy person starts to grumble when told to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes round' sounds like waking, but it puts M inside DO ROUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The dormouse is famous for hibernating and dozing, as at the Mad Hatter's tea party.

clue.text: NI party holds bizarre rally

indicators.note: holds means contains inside

parts.note: DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish party holds a strange gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To drum up support is to rally or gather it.
